hypothesis: Fifteen-minute directional alignment may explain outcomes among side-aligned-book candidates withheld only by the completed 5-minute BREAKOUT requirement, but the first predeclared opposed-context deployable path was a net winner and therefore directional alignment is not supported as an execution veto.
decision: Reject promotion of the 15-minute alignment hypothesis to an execution gate, veto, ranker, or sizing input. Preserve the authorized v14 runtime, exact 5-minute breakout requirement, sizing, exits, and execution scope unchanged. Keep 15-minute context as report-only attribution telemetry while accumulating independent deployable evidence in both long and short directions. The opposed-context HYPE short resolved positive after estimated costs and directly met revision 10's weakening falsifier; the aligned SOL loss remains mechanism-only because the live SOL position occupied the symbol.
falsifier: This rejection of a 15-minute execution veto would be updated only if a larger predeclared deployable sample includes both long and short sides and shows stable, after-cost separation in which aligned paths remain positive without one-path concentration while neutral and opposed paths are consistently worse. Evidence from occupied symbols, overlapping paths, retrospective slicing, or one direction alone is insufficient.
limitations: Only two prospective HYPE paths resolved, both are shorts, and their combined after-cost result is negative; no repeatable or bidirectional edge is established.
The positive opposed-context HYPE path weakens the proposed 15-minute veto but one observation cannot establish that opposition is favorable.
Both SOL paths conflict with an occupied live SOL position and therefore remain mechanism-only rather than deployable portfolio evidence.
Recorded BBO, top-level capacity, taker fees, and official funding estimate rather than prove private IOC execution and latency.
The fixed 60-minute challenger tests entry selection rather than the deployed 8-to-24-hour exit controller.
The same-run retrospective context slices in revision 10 remain hypothesis-formation evidence and are not pooled with this prospective schedule.
Fifteen-minute context remains descriptive telemetry only and cannot gate, veto, rank, size, route, close, or promote a trade.
No live strategy, position, order, stop, target, sizing policy, backend process, or portfolio configuration changed as a result of this revision.
